classification.summary: Vyper 0.2.15-0.3.0 emitted a malfunctioning reentrancy lock, letting remove_liquidity reenter add_liquidity and corrupt the CRV/ETH pool's balances; the defect lived in the compiler and lay dormant in immutable pool code for ~1.7 years.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/curve.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.
The executing code artifact and its code hash have not been established in structured evidence.
One or more target block, transaction, ordering, or creator anchors remain unresolved.

sources.note: onchain review (no exploit tx: incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> ethereum block 17805708, 2023-07-30T12:00:00Z). The CRV/ETH crypto pool 0x8301AE4fc9c624d1D396cbDAa1ed877821D7C511 was created at block 13676995, 2021-11-24T11:35:58Z. Curve v2 pools are immutable Vyper contracts and this one is confirmed so onchain: zero DELEGATECALL opcodes in the runtime, no EIP-1967 Upgraded event, and a byte-identical eth_getCode at the creation block and the incident block. Deployment basis is exact - the defect lived in the Vyper 0.2.15-0.3.0 compiler's reentrancy locks, dormant in unchanged bytecode for ~613 days.

onchain review: merged with the duplicate Curve_exp02 record for the same pool. Loss re-derived from the exploit tx rather than the $70m event-wide headline, which spans several pools: the pool's ETH balance fell 11,212.8724 -> 3,532.3787 (7,680.4937 ETH x $1,877.17) and it lost 7,193,401.7753 CRV (x $0.7018), = $19,465,922 at the incident block (DefiLlama)

limitations: Classification and loss came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/curve.json; legacy measurement.status=OK is provenance only.
The legacy USD loss lacks uniformly structured valuation provenance.
